title: The Nephandi's aim
summary: What sets the Fallen apart from other mages.

claims.text: A Nephandus is an Awakened soul who chose, in this life or an earlier one, to serve darkness and the Void, and that choice cannot be undone.
All of them work toward the end of Creation; they seek neither to rule the world nor to reunite Prime.
They count Traditions and Conventions as equally hostile, though they will pretend to side with either when it serves them.

title: Widderslainte who Awaken alone
summary: Fallen souls found by no Nephandus.

claims.text: Some widderslainte Awaken without any Nephandus finding them; many burn out in cruel experiments that take others with them, while a few learn alone and grow very dangerous.
A handful are taken in by kind or ally-hungry Tradition mages and may live inside a Tradition for a long time, but their nature always wins out.
Nephandi call on the Qlippothic Spheres, the dark mirror of the usual nine, which gives their magic a crueler and more brutal cast.
Qlippothic Correspondence reasons that if all things are linked, destroying one wounds the rest; its users tear holes in space or devour the gap between two places to cross it.

title: Abandoned Labyrinths
summary: Old Nephandi strongholds left on Earth.

claims.text: Most Nephandi were driven past the Horizon in 1945, leaving centuries of building behind; a few strongholds were found and burned, but most never were.
These Labyrinths now sit decaying in jungles and other harsh places, their guardians loose and their wards fading, and one by one their builders are coming back.
Every Labyrinth has some maze-like feature, whether to baffle attackers or in echo of the great Labyrinth of the Dark Umbra.

title: Marauder magic
summary: Why mad mages are so dangerous.

claims.text: Marauders reshape the world around them with vulgar magic and suffer none of the Paradox that binds other mages, so they can outmatch Tradition mages of equal skill.
Their helpers tend to be goblins, twisted mutants or other strangely reshaped beings and spirit creatures.

title: Infernalists among the monsters
summary: Damned beings that are not human.

claims.text: Some vampires, shapeshifters and other creatures also serve demons and dark gods, but they rarely ally with human or Awakened Infernalists, since many serve rival masters.
Infernal vampires treat mortal Infernalists as disposable pawns, and damned shapeshifters often seem closer to the Nephandi, many of them warped or maddened.
The Technocracy nearly always calls Umbrood aliens or extra-dimensional threats and meets them with hostility, which the spirits return.
Its standing order is to subjugate them before they can subjugate humanity, and the Void Engineers hold most of the Union's knowledge of such beings.
